metadata.question: Was the PM2.5 level higher in February 2020 than in February 2019 within a 50km radius of (40.923221, 104.238631)?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about PM2.5 levels in February 2020 vs February 2019 within a 50km radius of (40.923221, 104.238631). For PM2.5 analysis in Google Earth Engine, I should use: 1. Data: COPERNICUS/S5P/OFFL/L3_AER_AI or COPERNICUS/S5P/NRTI/L3_AER_AI for aerosol index as a proxy for PM2.5 2. Location: Create a 50km buffer around the point (40.923221, 104.238631) 3. Time: February 2019 vs February 2020 4. Processing: Calculate mean aerosol index for each period and compare Let me structure this: 1. Create geometry - point with 50km buffer 2. Get S5P aerosol data for both periods 3. Check collection sizes 4. Calculate mean aerosol index for each period 5. Compare and determine answer I need to handle: - Collection size checks (C1 if no data) - Valid pixel checks (C2 if no pixels after processing) - Valid result checks (C3 if invalid calculation) - Comparison logic for A/B answer ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const center = ee.Geometry.Point([104.238631, 40.923221]); const region = center.buffer(50000); // 50km radius // Define time periods for comparison const period1 = ['2019-02-01', '2019-02-28']; // Feb 2019 const period2 = ['2020-02-01', '2020-02-29']; // Feb 2020 // 2. Data Acquisition - Using Sentinel-5P Aerosol Index as PM2.5 proxy const getCollection = (startDate, endDate) => { return ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S5P/OFFL/L3_AER_AI') .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filterBounds(region) .select('absorbing_aerosol_index'); }; const col1 = getCollection(period1[0], period1[1]); const col2 = getCollection(period2[0], period2[1]); // Check collection sizes const size1 = col1.size().getInfo(); const size2 = col2.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Feb 2019 Images: ${size1}`); console.log(`Feb 2020 Images: ${size2}`); if (size1 === 0 || size2 === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // 3. Processing - Calculate mean images and statistics const mean1 = col1.mean(); const mean2 = col2.mean(); // Calculate pixel counts and mean values const stats1 = mean1.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean().combine({ reducer2: ee.Reducer.count(), sharedInputs: true }), geometry: region, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }); const stats2 = mean2.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean().combine({ reducer2: ee.Reducer.count(), sharedInputs: true }), geometry: region, scale: 1000, maxPixels: 1e9 }); const val1 = stats1.get('absorbing_aerosol_index_mean').getInfo(); const count1 = stats1.get('absorbing_aerosol_index_count').getInfo(); const val2 = stats2.get('absorbing_aerosol_index_mean').getInfo(); const count2 = stats2.get('absorbing_aerosol_index_count').getInfo(); console.log(`Feb 2019: AI=${val1?.toFixed(3)}, Pixels=${count1}`); console.log(`Feb 2020: AI=${val2?.toFixed(3)}, Pixels=${count2}`); // 4. Validation & Final Answer if (count1 === 0 || count2 === 0) { console.log("C2"); return; } if (val1 === null || val2 === null || !isFinite(val1) || !isFinite(val2)) { console.log("C3"); return; } // Compare PM2.5 proxy values (higher aerosol index = higher PM2.5) if (val2 > val1) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
